analysis.evidence: God is the subject, and אֶת־נֹחַ וְאֶת־בָּנָיו identifies Noah and his sons as the recipients. God expresses the blessing in the words פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ וּמִלְאוּ אֶת־הָאָרֶץ, “Be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth.”
analysis.morphology: Piel wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.
analysis.sense: to bless living creatures with fruitfulness

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיְבָרֶךְ (“he blessed”) and remains the subject of וַיֹּאמֶר (“he said”). Both verbs are masculine singular. God blesses Noah and his sons and then speaks to them.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute common noun with singular agreement.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיְבָרֶךְ ‘blessed’. The marked אֶת introduces נֹחַ ‘Noah’ as the first direct object. וְאֶת בָּנָיו ‘and his sons’ adds the second.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In אֶת נֹחַ וְאֶת בָּנָיו, “Noah and his sons,” אֶת marks Noah as a direct object of וַיְבָרֶךְ, “he blessed.” The singular suffix on בָּנָיו refers to Noah as their father.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים continues as the subject, and לָהֶם identifies Noah and his sons as the addressees. The plural imperatives פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ וּמִלְאוּ give the words God spoke to them.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

draft.change: Add Genesis 9:1 as evidence for the existing Hebrew sense le-to.
draft.definition: With a verb of speaking, לְ marks the person addressed.
draft.evidence: Genesis 9:1 names Noah and his sons and then identifies them as the hearers with וַיֹּאמֶר לָהֶם, “he said to them.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר לָהֶם, “he said to them,” the suffix refers back to Noah and his sons, whom God has just blessed. The plural commands פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ, “be fruitful and multiply,” address that same group.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ takes the form לָ־ before the third-person masculine plural pronominal suffix הֶם.
analysis.sense: Marks the people to whom speech is directed.

analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ ‘and’ precedes רְבוּ, a Qal imperative in the second person masculine plural.

analysis.morphology: Qal imperative, second person masculine plural, prefixed with the conjunction וּ.

analysis.evidence: In וּמִלְאוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ, “and fill the earth,” אֶת marks הָאָרֶץ (“the earth”) as the definite direct object of the imperative וּמִלְאוּ.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וּמִלְאוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ, “and fill the earth,” אֶת marks הָאָרֶץ as the direct object. The commands to Noah and his sons to be fruitful and multiply give it the broad sense of the earth they are to populate.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ־ precedes a common noun of both genders in the singular absolute state.
